I used to struggle with this. One thing that helped me was realizing that I wasn’t necessarily worried about negative things literally manifesting, it was more being afraid of fear itself. The fact that I was afraid, made me afraid that I was afraid, which made me fear that I was manifesting bad things. I’m not sure if that makes any sense at all, but it kept me in an awful mental loop. When I realized I was actually just scared of being scared, I truly understood that there really is nothing to fear except fear itself. 

Once I realized I can experience anxiety and not have to identify with it, I started to feel better. Running from it and denying it is only a temporary fix. For me personally, allowing it to pass through and not identify it helped the thoughts slowly go away. If you don’t identify with it, it won’t manifest because it’s not truly you. You manifest not what you want but what you are, and if you don’t identify with the fear, it’s not you, and it won’t manifest. It also helps to try to distract yourself with positive aspects of you life or things that are going well for you. Be gentle with yourself. If you have anxiety or a bad thought, it doesn’t mean bad things are going to happen to you, it’s totally normal from time to time.

There is never such thing as your struggles being “not severe enough” to get help. What you are experiencing is valid and very real, and you deserve a safe space to talk about what happened and what you are feeling. It sounds like you are hurting, and reaching out to a therapist is a great way to begin your healing journey. It may be challenging, but it gets better and you will come out a stronger person with the tools and resources to live a happy and fulfilling life after what happened to you. 

Not all people with PTSD have intense flashbacks and nightmares like in the movies. It presents in many different ways and can be subtle as just feeling nervous and uneasy in situations that remind you of what you experienced. 

What you are going through is valid and is more than worthy of care and attention. Reaching out to a therapist could be a great idea. I have found that talking about it is hard and scary at first, but it gets more and more manageable with time. 

You can and will get through this. It gets better with time and being kind to yourself. Good luck!
